pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/42596

In pre 5.0 .NET versions, when calling `Activity.AddBaggage`, will add a new Baggage item to internal linked list. The list was LIFO, which means when calling `Activity.Baggage` it will return the list in the reverse order of the added items. Also,  `Activity.AddBaggage` allow adding 2 items with same key and when calling `Activity.GetBaggageItem` to get a Baggage item value for a key which has duplication in the list, the API will return the last added item with that key. 

In 5.0, we used the internal LinkedList for other new scenarios (e.g. AddEvent) which required to have the list maintained on the order of the input. This had a side effect on `Baggage` order. The Baggage order became FIFO. Also, affected `Activity.GetBaggageItem` which made it to return the first added item with the specified input key instead of last added items. 

This is important to fix because `Baggage` is intended to be serialized over the wire across the process/machine. Looks users assumed specific order of the list even we didn't document the behavior. The change here is to ensure the old behavior to avoid breaking anyone and allow services using different version of the `System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource` to communicate reliably through serializing/deserializing the Baggage list.

issue_context.title: No way to update or remove item in Activity.Baggage
issue_context.body:
**Problem description:**

I need to update the value of an item in `Activity.Baggage`.
Initially, I've assumed that `Activity.AddBaggage` would replace the previous value, but it adds a second item with the same key and also does it in an inconsistent way, for example following code:
```CSharp
Console.WriteLine("Version={0}", Environment.Version);

var key = "Key1";
var activity = new Activity("Test").Start();
activity.AddBaggage(key, "1");
activity.AddBaggage(key, "2");
Console.WriteLine("Current value {0}={1}", key, activity.GetBaggageItem(key));

Console.WriteLine("All baggage values:");
var index = 0;
foreach (var pair in activity.Baggage)
{
    Console.WriteLine("[{0}] => {1}={2}", index++, pair.Key, pair.Value);
}
```
When you target `netcoreapp3.1` will output:
```
Version=3.1.7
Current value Key1=2
All baggage values:
[0] => Key1=2
[1] => Key1=1
```
And for `net5.0`:
```
Version=5.0.0
Current value Key1=1
All baggage values:
[0] => Key1=1
[1] => Key1=2
```
In additional to that when you are passing `Activity` baggage as a header in web request to Kestrel, `Activity` inside server would have order reverced so value for the same key on client and server would be diffirent.

**Suggested solution**
From my point of view having two items with the same key is an incorrect state of the `Activity`, it creates confusion, lead to strange errors (since users don't expect that order is important) and also increase size or the `Baggage`(that should be kept as small as posible).

Ideally `AddBaggage` method should remove or replace previous value. 
If you want to avoid adding performance overhead to `AddBaggage` method then it would be helpful to have some option of removing value from collection, for example `RemoveBaggage(string key)`. Then users could remove old value before adding to avoid mentioned problems.

CC @noahfalk 

This is the original design for AddBaggage, it always add. The only workaround for that is to clone the Activity object with updated Baggages. 

In 5.0 we have allowed the requested functionality for Tags through SetTag().

I understand that Add should only add values, but what's the point of adding items that won't be returned from GetBaggageItem and just increase collection.

Is it possible to add SetBaggage in the future? 

I think it's even more needed for Baggage then for Tags, since Baggage should be small and it's transferred in headers where order could be changed.

If it's intended behavior maybe you should specify that order is part of the contract (then we could request asp .net core and other implementations that parse header into baggage to preserve order).

Also will diffidence in ordering would be fixed in net5.0? (In netcoreapp3.1 it added to the beginning and in net5.0 to the end)

> but what's the point of adding items that won't be returned from GetBaggageItem and just increase collection.

You can get the whole list from `Activity.Baggage` property. So, it is possible to reach any item there.

> Is it possible to add SetBaggage in the future?

Yes, it is possible. we just need to track that request. you can notice I have added the `api-suggestion` label to this issue.

> I think it's even more needed for Baggage then for Tags, since Baggage should be small and it's transferred in headers where order could be changed.

Could you please add more details about your scenario? how you are using the Baggage and why you need to update or delete any item there?

> If it's intended behavior maybe you should specify that order is part of the contract (then we could request asp .net core and other implementations that parse header into baggage to preserve order).

We learned from other projects (e.g. `OpenTelemetry`) that order is important in sme scenarios. So we are maintaining the order as the items get added. The reason is the consumer or us in the future can put some limits to the number of items can be added to the list.
We may consider add somethign to the doc to clarify that.

> Also will diffidence in ordering would be fixed in net5.0? 

It is too late for .NET 5.0, and I think moving forward we'll keep the current order behavior. But we can consider adding `SetBaggage()` if we see some demand on it.

> You can get the whole list from Activity.Baggage property. So, it is possible to reach any item there.

Yes, but with different ordering between versions, it's complicated to understand what item was added last. It would probably be better in the future since you've agreed on a single ordering but between 3 and 5 it would be close to imposible.

> It is too late for .NET 5.0, and I think moving forward we'll keep the current behavior.

I assume the behavior of `GetBaggageItem` won't be changed in the future also? `netcoreapp3.1` behaved more logical to my taste since `GetBaggageItem` returned the last added item and after `net5.0` it's always the first added item ignoring subsequent adds.

> Could you please add more details about your scenario? how you are using the Baggage and why you need to update or delete any item there?

We are migrating from the custom correlation tracking system and adding it's correlation id as a baggage item. Unfortunately, it's done in a way that id assigned initially could be overridden by another value (provided as a header from incoming request for example). In a chain with multiple services calling each other baggage quickly becoming huge getting additional correlation id on each subsequent request. I understand that it's not in any way ideal architecture, but we need some period of our curstom correlation and activity working simultaneously since we could not migrate all service at once. 

In general I think any scenario that allows multiple calls of `AddBaggageItem` could hit this problem.

Thanks for the info @AndreyTretyak! Is your scenario above with AddBaggageItem() and GetBaggageItem() happening within the same process, or the two calls happen in different processes with the baggage already traveling over the wire?

Ignoring potential framework side fixes for the moment, if you need to get something working right now perhaps a workaround like this is a good short term solution?
1. Where the code currently calls AddBaggage(), instead call SetCustomProperty(). SetCustomProperty has replacement semantics so GetCustomProperty() will always return whatever was the last value you set.
2. Just prior to stopping/disposing the Activity, use GetCustomProperty() to retrieve whatever the final value was intended to be, then call AddBaggage() with that value.


@tarekgh - it sounds like we have unintentionally created a compat break between v3 and v5? I am guessing we never specified what the ordering would be in the past, but GetBaggageItem() made it easy for users to take the dependency implicitly. I can follow up with you offline to figure out where potential compat breaks fall relative to our current bug bar.

Thank you for the suggestion @noahfalk . In our case AddBaggageItem() and GetBaggageItem() mostly happening in separate processes. 
Because of this, the fact that Kestrel reverses the order of baggage in net core 3.1 complicates things. From what I've seen in code it should be fine for net 5.0 since you've changed the addition order (probably that was the reason for order change).

Problem with using `SetCustomProperty()` is that it won't be transferred (as far as I understand) to nested activities or outgoing requests and that's the main reason for using baggage over tags. 

Custom properties would be a nice replacement of Tags after we'll move to net5.0 (or we could use `SetTag` then), since we have a similar scenario of adding a state (success/failure) to activity tags that could be later overridden (ex. in case of exception).

Curently for the scenario with tags we could probably do some kind of logic that would return the last tag pair with required key (althougth I dislike the idea of having huge list of useles values in tags), and then reverse this logic to return the first tag after moving to net5.0. But with baggage, it's more complicated since I don't see a way of understanding right order if services use diffirent frameworks, like Servise1(net core 3.1) -> Service2 (net5.0) -> Service3(net472), only adding indexes to keys :), but so many duplicates would explode the size of the baggage quite quick.

So it looks hopeless, but if you have any suggestions about making simular scenario work on net core 3.1, they would be grately appreciated. I'm very tempted to use reflection for the removal of old pair :)

@tarekgh  thank you for looking into this. I think fixing the behavior of `GetBaggageItem` should cover most of our scenarios. There would be still an issue of increasing baggage with each add, but that's a much smaller problem and it's kind of our fault for misunderstanding the contract. Althought, it would be very useful if in some future version you could provide ability to remove or replace baggage items.

In our case, we are controling the version of the packages in all of them so it would be great if NuGet package would containe updated behaivour. I've assumed there would be no packages after net5.0 so it's great that you would continue publishing them, thank you.

@AndreyTretyak I have opened the PR https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/42659 (this is against 6.0) to go back to old behavior of Baggages. After we merge this one, I'll try to get this change to 5.0 too if it get approved.
@ericstj @jeffhandley this is another candidate fix to port to 5.0 release. I'll CC you on the porting PR after I process this one.
Thanks for the heads-up, @tarekgh. From what I can tell, this wouldn't block RC2 but would be _considered_ for GA/RTM.  Let me know if you were thinking otherwise.
@jeffhandley having it for GA/RTM will be fine.

review_comments: We should probably add a test that confirms baggage enumeration ordering is consistent (across versions) when multiple Activities in a chain have all had baggage added. Looking at the code it appears we have always maintained the order that child activity baggage is enumerated before parent activity baggage.
